public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI has about three quarters to prove itself before a collapse that will savage the revenues of the largest tech companies.
conditions: unless AI proves itself within three quarters

statement.excerpt: I believe that artificial intelligence has three quarters to prove itself before the apocalypse comes, and when it does, it will be that much worse, savaging the revenues of the biggest companies in tech.

from_speaker: savaging the revenues of the biggest companies in tech
our_interpretation: Following the supplied conditional reading, the antecedent is AI failing to prove itself within three quarters. That antecedent must be established independently of whether revenues later fell.
The proving window ends December 31, 2024, the latest end of the next three calendar quarters. A literal nine-month reading would end December 18, 2024.
The ordinary reading of 'savaging' is severe, widespread revenue damage caused by an AI-demand collapse. No arbitrary percentage is imposed.
The context names Nvidia, Google, Amazon, Snowflake and Microsoft as exposed companies, but does not fix a complete company basket.
The three-quarter deadline clearly governs the proving window; the lag between a collapse and its full revenue effects is unspecified.
The claim specifies neither an accounting basis nor a financial source.
criteria.support_condition: After independently establishing that AI failed the intended proof test by the deadline, evidence shows an AI-demand collapse causing severe revenue declines across the relevant large technology companies.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After independently establishing the same antecedent, revenue and demand evidence over the intended aftermath shows that the predicted collapse and severe revenue damage did not occur.
